primary_source.title: Amplituhedra and origami, I: tree level
primary_source.author: Pavel Galashin

source_definition.geometric_edge_weight: For an edge e dual to {g1*,g2*}, the geometric edge weight is the Euclidean length |xhat(g1*)-xhat(g2*)|.
source_definition.gauge_equivalence: wt' is gauge equivalent to wt when wt'(e)=g(w) wt(e) g(b) for e={w,b}, with g=1 at every boundary vertex.
source_definition.TE3: A t-immersion/t-embedding of (Gamma,wt) requires wt and the Euclidean geometric edge weights to be gauge equivalent.

source_locations: Section 1.2, geometric edge-weight definition and gauge equivalence

current_c05.registered_statement: The five retained algebraic witnesses extend to five planar t-embeddings satisfying the recorded boundary and geometric constraints.
current_c05.missing_source_definition_check: No TE3 gauge-equivalence check between the protected graph weights and Euclidean dual-edge lengths is recorded in the evidence.

decision_rule: If TE3 fails for the retained C04 weight class, the evidence supports planar algebraic Kenyon-Smirnov realizations with the listed geometric properties, not t-embeddings of that protected weighted graph in the source-defined sense.
